mainTopic: Do kosher and non-kosher נבלות join together to make a כזית, for טומאה and for the איסור of eating?
overview: The משנה taught that all נבלות join together to make a כזית. רב limits this to טומאה: for the איסור of eating, kosher and non-kosher carcasses stay separate. לוי says they join even for eating. רב אסי says kosher and non-kosher stay separate, and there are two versions of whether he argues with רב. The גמרא challenges רב אסי from a ברייתא about a dead cow and a live camel. It first answers that the ברייתא means two live animals join, following רבי יהודה on אבר מן החי. That answer is pushed back twice: the ברייתא's example would be pointless, and a second ברייתא says cow and camel join 'whether alive or dead.' Finally the גמרא answers for רב אסי that the ברייתא follows a תנא who holds איסור חל על איסור, which רב אסי does not hold.

steps.title: The joining rule applies only to טומאה, not to eating
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the משנה's rule that all נבלות join together. It applies only to טומאה. For the איסור of eating, kosher and non-kosher carcasses stay separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule that all carcasses join together was taught only about ritual impurity. For eating, kosher carcasses count by themselves and non-kosher carcasses count by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a limit on the משנה's rule that all נבלות combine. They combine for טומאה, but not for the איסור of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be טמא you need a כזית of נבלה, and the משנה lets pieces from different animals add up. רב says this mixing works only for טומאה. For the eating prohibition, a half-כזית of kosher נבלה cannot add up with a half-כזית of non-kosher נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about…; a formula that limits a rule
With regard to ritual impurity
With regard to the איסור of eating
Here: kosher animals (literally 'pure ones')
Here: non-kosher animals (literally 'impure ones')

steps.confusionAlert: Here טהורין and טמאים mean kosher and non-kosher animals. They do not mean pure and impure objects, even though the line is talking about טומאה.

phrases.english: They taught this only with regard to ritual impurity,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה's rule that all נבלות join together.

phrases.english: but with regard to eating,
kosher ones are by themselves,
and non-kosher ones are by themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the משנה's rule that all carcasses join
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kosher and non-kosher carcasses join for טומאה but not for the איסור of eating

steps.title: לוי says they join even for eating
steps.stepSummary: לוי disagrees with רב. He holds that kosher and non-kosher carcasses join together even for the איסור of eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי says: even for eating, they join together.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, לוי, gives the opposite view. The joining works for eating too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב split the two areas: they join for טומאה but not for eating. לוי does not split them. In his view, a half-כזית of kosher נבלה plus a half-כזית of non-kosher נבלה add up to a full כזית for the eating prohibition as well.

keyTerms.meaning: They join together (to reach the minimum amount)
Even… also; extends the rule to a further case

phrases.english: And Levi says:
Even for eating, they also join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵוִי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לַאֲכִילָה נָמֵי מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kosher and non-kosher carcasses join even for the איסור of eating

steps.title: רב אסי says kosher and non-kosher stay separate
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that kosher carcasses count by themselves and non-kosher carcasses count by themselves. He does not say whether he means only eating or טומאה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי says: kosher ones by themselves, and non-kosher ones by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion is brought: רב אסי keeps kosher and non-kosher carcasses separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's words are short and general. He does not say whether he is talking only about eating, like רב, or about טומאה as well. That unclear point is what the next step deals with.

keyTerms.meaning: By themselves; they count only with their own kind

phrases.english: And Rav Asi says:
Kosher ones are by themselves,
and non-kosher ones are by themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: טְהוֹרִים לְעַצְמָן וּטְמֵאִין לְעַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion on the same question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kosher and non-kosher carcasses do not join (the scope is left unclear)

steps.title: Two versions: does רב אסי argue with רב?
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב אסי argues with רב, meaning he holds they stay separate even for טומאה. Others say he does not argue and is only talking about eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he disagrees with רב, and some say he does not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two versions of how to understand רב אסי. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב אסי argues with רב, then he holds kosher and non-kosher carcasses never join, not even for טומאה. If he does not argue, he agrees they join for טומאה and only stay separate for eating, which is exactly רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It (his statement) disagrees

phrases.english: There are those who say: he disagrees with Rav,
and there are those who say: he does not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies how far רב אסי's statement reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Version one: רב אסי keeps them separate even for טומאה. Version two: he agrees with רב.

steps.title: Challenge from the dead cow and live camel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a dead cow and a live camel do not join. That implies two dead animals, one kosher and one not, do join. This contradicts רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a teaching: the carcass of a cow and flesh from a live camel do not join together. This implies that if both are dead, they do join. That is a difficulty for רב אסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אסי, in the version where he argues with רב, using an inference from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cow is kosher and a camel is not. The ברייתא says the only reason they don't join is that one is dead and the other alive, which implies two dead ones would join. רב can explain that as being about טומאה, but רב אסי holds kosher and non-kosher never join, so the ברייתא seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead body of
From a living (animal)
This implies; introduces an inference from the wording

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The carcass of a cow and the flesh of a live camel
do not join with one another.
This implies that if both are dead, they join,
and this is difficult for Rav Asi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the version in which רב אסי argues with רב
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי, in the version where he argues with רב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies two dead animals, one kosher and one not, join together. That goes against keeping kosher and non-kosher separate.

steps.title: Read it as both alive, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the inference: what the ברייתא implies is that two live animals join. This follows רבי יהודה, who holds that אבר מן החי applies even to a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: this implies that if both are alive, they join. And whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה, who says the איסור of a limb from a living animal applies to a non-kosher animal too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא's hidden implication differently. It then says which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's point is not that two dead animals join. Its point is that flesh from two live animals, a cow and a camel, joins. That works only for someone who holds the אבר מן החי prohibition applies to a non-kosher camel just as it does to a kosher cow, which is רבי יהודה. So the ברייתא says nothing about two dead carcasses, and רב אסי is no longer contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; reread the source
And who is (the תנא of this teaching)?
A limb taken from a living animal, which is forbidden to eat
Applies to a non-kosher animal

steps.confusionAlert: בַּטְּמֵאָה here means 'to a non-kosher animal.' It has nothing to do with טומאה, ritual impurity.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: kosher and non-kosher carcasses join for טומאה, not for eating. לוי: they join for both. רב אסי: they stay separate. This step tries to defend רב אסי by reading the cow-and-camel ברייתא as 'both alive join,' following רבי יהודה. The next steps push back on this answer, and a different answer comes in Step 9.

phrases.english: Say instead: this implies that if both are alive, they join,
and whose view is it? It is Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי נוֹהֵג בַּטְּמֵאָה.
phrases.english: who says: the prohibition of a limb from a living animal applies to a non-kosher animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב אסי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the inference and assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא implies that two dead animals, kosher and non-kosher, join
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא implies that two live animals join, following רבי יהודה's view on אבר מן החי

steps.title: Why mention a dead cow and a live camel if even two dead ones do not join?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 6. If two dead animals do not join, the ברייתא's case of a dead cow and a live camel is pointless. The simpler case would already teach that they do not join.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about when both are dead? Do they not join? If so, why does the ברייתא go out of its way to teach 'a dead cow and a live camel'? Even if both were dead, they would not join!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave for רב אסי. If two dead animals do not join, the ברייתא picked a strange, needlessly extreme example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6 the גמרא said the ברייתא's hidden lesson is that two live animals join, while two dead ones do not. But if two dead ones do not join, the ברייתא could have used that simpler case to teach that they don't join. Choosing a dead cow with a live camel suggests that two dead animals would join, which goes against רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? A question asking why the text chose this example
He 'runs and teaches.' The תנא goes out of his way to a more unusual case

phrases.english: But if both of them are dead, what is the law?
Do they not join together?
If so, why specifically
does he run and teach
'a dead cow and a live camel'?
phrases.notes: This is the wording of the ברייתא from Step 5.

phrases.english: After all, even if both of them are dead
they do not join together!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מַאי אִירְיָא דְּרָהֵיט וְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 6 by showing that it makes the ברייתא's choice of example pointless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 6, that the ברייתא only implies that two live animals join, while two dead animals do not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא does not pick an extreme, mixed case if a simpler case teaches the same lesson. Picking dead-cow-with-live-camel suggests that two dead animals would join.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says two dead animals do join
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא. It says half a כזית from a live cow and half from a dead camel do not join, but cow and camel join 'whether alive or dead.' To avoid an internal contradiction, the second clause must mean both alive or both dead. So two dead animals join, against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it was taught in a ברייתא: Half a כזית from a cow while it is alive and half a כזית from a camel after it died do not join. But half a כזית from a cow and half a כזית from a camel, whether alive or dead, do join. The first part seems to contradict the second part! So isn't it clear from this that when both are dead, they join?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge to רב אסי. It brings a ברייתא that seems to say directly that a dead kosher animal and a dead non-kosher animal join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause says a live cow and a dead camel do not join. If the second clause, 'whether alive or dead,' meant any mix, it would contradict the first clause. So it must mean both alive or both dead, and that means two dead animals do join. This is the opposite of רב אסי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Half an olive's volume. Not enough on its own to be punished for eating, so the question is whether two halves add up
The first clause of a ברייתא or משנה
The last clause of a ברייתא or משנה
Learn from it. Used to draw a conclusion from a source

steps.confusionAlert: 'Whether alive or dead' does NOT mean one alive and one dead. The first clause already said that mix does not join. It means both alive or both dead.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught in a ברייתא:
Half an olive-bulk from a cow while it is alive
and half an olive-bulk from a camel after it died
do not join together.
But half an olive-bulk from a cow
and half an olive-bulk from a camel,
whether alive or dead,
do join together.
The first clause contradicts the last clause!
phrases.notes: If 'alive or dead' allowed a mix, it would clash with the first line. So it has to mean both the same.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it clear from this:
when both are dead, they join together!?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge on top of Step 7, this time from a ברייתא that seems to state the opposite of רב אסי's ruling directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 6 answer that the first ברייתא only teaches that two live animals join, and with it רב אסי's ruling (Step 3) that kosher and non-kosher carcasses are counted separately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only way to read the ברייתא without contradiction is that two dead animals join. That directly opposes רב אסי.

steps.title: רב אסי: this תנא holds that one prohibition can land on another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers on רב אסי's behalf: the ברייתא follows a תנא who holds איסור חל על איסור. In that view the נבילה prohibition also applies to a camel, which is already forbidden, so both halves are the same איסור and join. רב אסי himself does not hold this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי could say to you: This תנא holds that a prohibition can take effect on something that is already forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי, saying what he could answer: the ברייתא follows a different opinion, not his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A camel is already forbidden because it is a non-kosher animal. This תנא holds that when it dies, the נבילה prohibition takes effect on it too, so both halves are forbidden as נבילה and they add up. רב אסי holds that a second prohibition does not take effect on something already forbidden. So for him the dead camel is forbidden only as a non-kosher animal, not as נבילה, and the two halves do not join.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition takes effect even on something that is already forbidden by another prohibition
A sage of the משנה era whose teaching is recorded in a משנה or ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Whether kosher and non-kosher carcasses join depends on whether איסור חל על איסור. If the נבילה prohibition lands on the non-kosher animal too, both are the same איסור and they join. If it doesn't, they stay separate, which is רב אסי's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the whole argument is not really about animals but about a basic rule: can a second איסור take effect on something that is already forbidden? That rule comes up all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: רב אסי could say to you:
This תנא holds
that a prohibition takes effect on another prohibition.
phrases.notes: So the נבילה prohibition lands on the camel too, even though it was already forbidden as non-kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by saying the ברייתא follows a different underlying rule than רב אסי holds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source follows a different opinion: the ברייתא belongs to a תנא with a different basic rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to prove, for everyone, that dead kosher and non-kosher animals join, which would refute רב אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only holds for a תנא who says איסור חל על איסור. רב אסי holds that a second איסור does not take effect, so in his view the two do not join.
